lastCompletedStory.title: Wrapper re-resolves model + effort per respawn via cam orch-resolve, with fail-safe fallback and divergence event

nextStoryContext: buildOrchestratorPaneCommand's respawn branch (src/commands/run.ts) now re-resolves model+effort on EVERY self-handoff respawn instead of re-execing the literal argv baked in at initial `cam run` build time. New OrchestratorPaneCommandOptions fields: `resolverCmd?: string` (shell command invoked at each respawn to re-resolve, defaulting to the bare 'cam orch-resolve' PATH lookup; the real setupPanes caller instead builds `${q(process.execPath)} ${q(process.argv[1] ?? 'cam')} orch-resolve`, a same-binary self-invoke mirroring forkMonitor's convention in src/retry/launcher.ts, robust against a stale/absent `cam` on PATH) and `eventsLogPath?: string` (defaults to the sibling of pidMarker, i.e. .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl). Inside the respawn branch, AFTER the fresh session-id is minted (uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z') and written to sessionIdMarker: `resolved=$(${resolverCmd} 2>/dev/null); newmodel=$(printf '%s' "$resolved" | jq -r '.model // empty'); neweffort=$(... '.effort // empty')`. Guard is a PLAIN command-failure check, never a bash timeout/watchdog (macOS bash 3.2.57 has no coreutils `timeout`; orch-resolve is a local TOML point-read so a hang is not a realistic failure mode): `if [ -n "$resolved" ] && [ -n "$newmodel" ] && [ -n "$neweffort" ]; then model="$newmodel"; effort="$neweffort"; else <fallback>; fi`. On any failure/absence/malformed-output, the `model`/`effort` bash variables are left untouched (last known-good: either the initial TS-side seed or a prior successful respawn's values) AND the wrapper still respawns claude on those values -- never bricks the session on a config typo. The fallback branch also appends ONE line to eventsLogPath via `jq -nc --arg ts ... --arg uuid "$sid" --arg model "$model" --arg effort "$effort" '{ts:$ts, uuid:$uuid, kind:"orch-resolve-fallback", detail:{phase:"orchestrator", model:$model, effort:$effort}}'` -- KEY-AND-SHAPE-identical (ts/uuid/kind/detail, storyId genuinely omitted not null) to a WorkerEvent written by the production `makeFileEventLogger` (src/supervisor/events.ts), whose WorkerEventKind union and WorkerEventDetail union both gained a new 'orch-resolve-fallback' entry paired with the OrchResolveFallbackEventDetail interface ({ phase: 'orchestrator', model: string, effort: string }). aggregateTokensPerIssue (src/stats/tokens.ts) ignores this kind safely (not 'tokens'/'cycle-tokens'), confirmed by test. The `--effort` capability gate from US-002 is UNCHANGED and remains the one-time build-time decision: whether the argv template mentions `--effort` AT ALL (an unrecognized flag is boot-fatal on an older claude build) never changes mid-session; only the VALUE flowing through an already-present clause is now live-reread. Two integration tests in test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts exercise this end-to-end via real spawnSync of the assembled bash against a stub claude on PATH: one drives the REAL `bun index.ts orch-resolve` against a staged+edited project.toml (proves live pickup), the other drives a hand-authored resolver stub that succeeds once then fails (proves fail-safe fallback + event shape parity). test/run.test.ts gained 5 new unit-level string-shape assertions covering the default/custom resolverCmd, the jq-parsed conditional guard, the fallback event's exact jq -nc invocation and default/custom eventsLogPath, and their relative ordering (resolver call after uuidgen+sessionIdMarker write; fallback event inside the else branch, before the reason-based counter update) -- none of the PRE-EXISTING ordering assertions in that describe block were weakened, only the two `--effort`-placement tests were updated from a literal `--effort '<value>'` shape to the seeded-bash-variable shape (`effort='<value>'` seed + `--effort "$effort"` read), matching the US-002 seam that test/commands/run-configpath-seam.test.ts and test/commands/run-effort-argv.test.ts also had to update for the same reason. src/commands/run.ts crossed 1052->1127, src/supervisor/events.ts crossed 876->904, and test/run.test.ts crossed 1054->1059 then 1059->1112 (5 new unit tests) -- all raised with tracker-ref-carrying `_ref` entries in scripts/file-size-budget.json.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed -n/--null-input runs the filter once against `null` without reading stdin (enables constructing a JSON object from scratch), -c/--compact-output emits one line per object, and --arg name value binds a STRING to $name in the filter. Matches the bash respawn wrapper's `jq -nc --arg ts ... --arg model "$model" ... '{ts:$ts, ..., detail:{model:$model, ...}}'` usage exactly: no numeric coercion assumed anywhere (model/effort are always treated as opaque strings, consistent with readPhaseEffort's string-tier contract).
